title: Discrimination case studies
subject: PSHE
source: Written for pshe/y8 lesson 6 (Discrimination case studies (pupil PDF))
intro: Lesson 6: Tackling racism and religious discrimination. Read the ideas from the lesson, then do the tasks.

panels.title: Definitions
points: Racism: unfair treatment due to race
Religious discrimination: due to faith or belief

bullets: Includes race and religion or belief
Illegal to discriminate at work, school, services

panels.title: Responding
points: Report to school; the police for hate crimes

passage.title: Case 1: the job interview
paras: Amina applies for a weekend job at a shop. At the interview, the manager says, 'We don't want staff in headscarves on the till.' She is not offered the job, although she has the most experience.

passage.title: Case 2: the café
paras: Daniel uses a wheelchair. A café refuses to let him in, saying the wheelchair 'gets in the way', although there is space and a ramp.

passage.title: Case 3: the football club
paras: Kwame is told he cannot join a local youth club team. The coach says, 'Players like you cause trouble,' and makes a comment about his skin colour.

passage.title: Case 4: the online shop
paras: Mr Ahmed, aged 68, is told he cannot apply for a delivery job 'because older people are too slow', without any test of what he can do.

questions.q: Case 1: what is the protected characteristic, and what should Amina do?
questions.a: Religion or belief. Keep a written note of what was said; complain to the company; get advice (for example from Citizens Advice or the Equality Advisory Support Service).

questions.q: Case 2: what is the protected characteristic, and what should happen?
questions.a: Disability. The café must make reasonable adjustments; Daniel can complain to the café and seek advice.

questions.q: Case 3: what is the protected characteristic, and what should Kwame do?
questions.a: Race. Tell a trusted adult, report it to the club's welfare officer or league; a hate incident can be reported to the police.

questions.q: Case 4: what is the protected characteristic?
questions.a: Age. Refusing a job because of age, without a fair test, is discrimination.

keywords.def: treating people unfairly because of race, colour or ethnicity
treating someone unfairly because of who they are
the UK law protecting people from discrimination
a feature the Equality Act protects, such as race or religion

questions.a: For example: race, religion or belief, disability.

questions.q: Core: Case studies (pupil PDF, fictional): identify the discrimination, the protected characteristic and the right response.
Extend: In the portal response box, write a paragraph: 'Islam teaches equality because...'
questions.a: Islam teaches equality because Allah created all people and judges by righteousness, not race (49:13), as the Prophet ﷺ taught in the Farewell Sermon.

questions.q: Stretch: Explain why protecting others' rights also protects Muslims' rights.
questions.a: The same law that protects others' beliefs protects ours; justice must be for all.

questions.q: Refusing someone a job because of their religion is...
options: Discrimination, illegal under the Equality Act 2010
questions.a: B) Discrimination, illegal under the Equality Act 2010. Religion or belief is a protected characteristic.

questions.q: The Equality Act 2010 protects... A) only adults B) nine characteristics including race and religion C) only football teams
questions.a: B) nine characteristics including race and religion
options: Nine characteristics including race and religion

questions.q: Big question: how should we respond to discrimination?
questions.a: Do not retaliate, record, report and support the target.
